subject: Edge route validation and NAT shadowing — live-impact (HAAS Systems)
messages:
From: John Durand <john.durand@haas-systems.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: edgeops@haas-systems.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:14:03 -0700
Subject: Intermittent failures after edge router update — production impact

Marcus —

We pushed the vendor OS update to the on-prem edge router (v5.2.11 -> v5.3.0) at 07:30 local and immediately started seeing sporadic failures from our app pods to Redwood Private endpoints. Symptoms: TCP connections tear down mid-stream with RSTs, occasional one-way traffic (customer->redwood OK, return drops), and very high retransmit counts. The issue is intermittent but heavily correlated to sessions that traverse the edge NAT pool bound for 203.0.113.0/24.

I've attached a short pcap and ifconfig output from the edge box.

Attachments: live-trace-20270521.pcap, ifconfig-edge-20270521.txt

Can you take a look? Our users are seeing 10–15% request failures.

—John
Network Ops, HAAS Systems
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: John Durand <john.durand@haas-systems.com>, edgeops@haas-systems.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:34:27 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent failures after edge router update — production impact

Folks — forwarding an urgent production connectivity report from HAAS after their edge OS upgrade. Symptoms sound like asymmetric return path + NAT translation churn. Key things to validate immediately:

- Route tables on their transit/edge devices (duplicate static vs. BGP learned).
- NAT conntrack table size / churn and any conntrack restart events around 07:30.
- Firewall/SG attachments on the private frontdoors that might drop ephemeral port ranges.
- MTU/MSS issues if packet sizes are being fragmented.

John attached a pcap and ifconfig; I pulled a few quick things from their notes and our frontdoor logs: I see spikes in SYN_RECV and a handful of RSTs referencing server IPs in 203.0.113.0/24 around the same minute range.

Immediate ask: Monica, can you draft a quick set of triage commands and run conntrack/iptables/synstat on the frontdoor and ask John for conntrack counters on their edge? Laura, can you review our route-policy for that customer prefix — I want to rule out any accidental shadowing of static routes leading to hairpinning.

I'll keep John in the loop; if we need a temporary mitigation we can push a limited SNAT rule on our frontdoor to stabilize sessions.

Thanks —
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: John Durand <john.durand@haas-systems.com>, edgeops@haas-systems.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:02:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent failures after edge router update — production impact

Marcus / team — quick update from frontdoor triage (ran against fd-west-2a):

What I checked:
- conntrack entries: count jumped from 42k -> 198k within minutes of 07:30 (conntrack table size 200k) and we saw ~6k FAILED entries (likely due to conntrack table probe/evictions).
- iptables -t nat -L: NAT MASQUERADE rule for customer prefix present, but I see a second static SNAT rule referencing an old appliance IP (10.254.12.7) that may cause translation mismatch when HAAS hairpins.
- tcpdump on frontdoor: observed SYN -> SYN/ACK then immediate RST from server side in ~18% of samples; TCP MSS in options shows 1460, but edge pcap shows fragments and occasional ICMP frag-needed messages.

Actions taken (temporary):
- Added iptables/ebtables rule to clamp MSS to 1400 on the FD interface: iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
- Inserted a temporary SNAT rule mapping the HAAS service CIDR to a local stable SNAT IP to avoid conntrack churn while we investigate (will remove ASAP): iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.20.0.0/16 -d 203.0.113.0/24 -j SNAT --to-source 10.10.200.45

Observed effect: within ~3 minutes retransmit rate dropped by ~60% in our sample window; HAAS reported fewer errors.

Attached: conntrack-snapshot-20270521.txt (conntrack dumps)

Next steps: get HAAS to confirm their edge has no duplicate static route to the same customer prefix and to share their conntrack counts. Laura — routing policy (your side) + BGP learned path check would be helpful.

—Monica
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: John Durand <john.durand@haas-systems.com>, edgeops@haas-systems.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:18:59 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent failures after edge router update — production impact

Thanks Monica — good catch. A few notes from routing/security side after a quick audit:

Findings:
- On HAAS side we see both a static route (admin-installed) AND a BGP-learned route to 203.0.113.0/24 with different next-hops and different AS path. When the router's control plane restarted during the upgrade it appears the static route intermittently won, causing traffic to hairpin to the older appliance (10.254.12.7) which no longer has appropriate SNAT mappings. That explains the RSTs and conntrack evictions.
- In our frontdoor config we had an egress security group rule permitting 0.0.0.0/0 ephemeral ports but an ACL on the NAT box unintentionally filtered some ephemeral ranges (32768-61000) to the older appliance. That policy mismatch increases the chances of broken return flows.

Proposed remediation plan (short + medium term):
1) Short: coordinate with HAAS to delete the stale static route or tie its admin to a next-hop with proper next-hop health checks. We can keep Monica's temporary SNAT in place for 2 hours while they patch.
2) Medium: update our route-policy to prefer BGP-learned paths for HAAS prefixes and add a community to tag and prefer stable next-hops; roll an ASF/BGP path-prep config change (will require 2-hour maintenance window).
3) Long: add a staged onboarding checklist to catch static vs BGP conflicts in customer-run routers (include conntrack thresholds), and automations to alert on sudden conntrack growth >+100% in 5m.

I've opened JIRA-PLAT-987 for the medium-term route-policy work and scheduled a coordination call with HAAS ops at 13:00 PT.

—Laura
Principal Network Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: John Durand <john.durand@haas-systems.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge route validation and NAT shadowing — live-impact (HAAS Systems)

John / team — thanks for the quick responses and the packet captures. Summary and next steps: 

Summary:
- Root cause: control-plane change during vendor OS upgrade caused HAAS to intermittently prefer a stale static route to 203.0.113.0/24, leading to hairpin to an older appliance with no matching SNAT state and sudden conntrack growth/evictions at our frontdoor. MTU/fragmentation amplified the failures.
- Immediate mitigation: Monica added MSS clamp (1400) and a temporary SNAT mapping; retransmits and error rate fell substantially.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- HAAS: remove the stale static route or update its next-hop so BGP is the active path (owner: John) — ETA: before 15:00 PT today.
- Monica: keep temporary SNAT/MSS clamp in place until HAAS confirms (owner: Monica) — ETA: rollback 2 hrs after confirmation.
- Laura: implement BGP-preference change and file JIRA-PLAT-987 for platform-level protection (owner: Laura) — ETA: schedule during next maintenance window (TBD).
- Marcus: coordinate postmortem and add static-vs-bgp check to onboarding checklist (owner: Marcus) — ETA: draft PMF by Monday.

I'll join the 13:00 PT call to coordinate. If HAAS confirms removal of the static route and we see continued stability, we'll close the incident; otherwise escalate to vendor for potential firmware rollback.

Thanks everyone —
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
